title: Olaparib after treatment for early breast cancer
context_label: Germline BRCA1/2-associated, HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer
scope_note: These materials cover olaparib after treatment for high-risk early breast cancer. Other cancers use different eligibility, duration and follow-up; use the matching NCCP indication and your treating team’s plan.
schedule_label: Olaparib tablets morning and evening, every day
schedule_summary: Take your prescribed olaparib dose morning and evening every day, without a planned rest week. This breast course lasts up to one year, or stops earlier if the cancer returns or side effects make treatment unsuitable. Prescribed endocrine therapy can continue on its own timetable.
purpose: Reduce the chance of invasive recurrence after standard chemotherapy and local treatment. It may be taken alongside prescribed endocrine therapy for hormone receptor-positive disease.
indication_text: NCCP 00588 h only: germline pathogenic BRCA1/2-associated HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer after neoadjuvant/adjuvant chemotherapy. Do not route other 00588 indications into this breast suite.
administration_text: The usual starting dose is 300 mg of olaparib tablets twice daily, with or without food. This breast course lasts up to one year, or stops earlier if the cancer returns or side effects make treatment unsuitable. Prescribed endocrine therapy can continue on its own timetable. Follow your own prescription if the dose changes.
monitoring_summary: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests every four weeks through the first 12 months; extra tests for symptoms or abnormal results. Review nausea, intake, fatigue, infection, bruising, breathing, medicines and tablet supply.
review_status: Source-reconciled feasibility draft; independent clinician, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending.

agents.name: Olaparib
agents.mechanism: Olaparib is a PARP inhibitor: it blocks proteins that help repair damaged DNA and can trap them on the DNA. Cancer cells with a harmful BRCA1 or BRCA2 change already have difficulty using an important repair pathway. Blocking PARP can leave more damage than these cells can repair. Normal blood-forming cells can also be affected, which explains why blood counts and symptom checks remain important during targeted treatment.
agents.explanation: Olaparib is a PARP inhibitor: it blocks proteins that help repair damaged DNA and can trap them on the DNA. Cancer cells with a harmful BRCA1 or BRCA2 change already have difficulty using an important repair pathway. Blocking PARP can leave more damage than these cells can repair. Normal blood-forming cells can also be affected, which explains why blood counts and symptom checks remain important during targeted treatment.
risks: Anaemia, sometimes requiring transfusion; low white cells or platelets with infection or bleeding risk
Nausea, vomiting, indigestion, diarrhoea, reduced appetite and changes in taste
Fatigue or weakness, headache, dizziness and mouth soreness
Serious persistent blood-count changes, including MDS/AML; the risk varies with the treatment setting and previous therapy
Pneumonitis: inflammation of the lungs that can be serious or fatal
Blood clots in veins or lungs; symptoms need urgent assessment
Liver injury and changes in kidney blood tests; the team may need to review treatment
Allergic reactions and harm to an unborn baby; discuss fertility, contraception and breastfeeding where relevant
agents.watch: Agree a written anti-sickness plan with your team, including what is prescribed regularly, what is for rescue, and when to call if it is not working. NCCP classifies oral olaparib as moderate-to-high sickness risk, but a fixed intravenous chemotherapy anti-sickness cycle does not apply. Some people need prescribed support and others do not need routine prevention. A stomach-acid medicine may be considered for symptoms under local policy.

anatomy: Fatigue, headache or dizziness can affect daily life. Marked tiredness, pallor, breathlessness or a fast heartbeat can also signal anaemia; report a change rather than assuming it is expected.
Taste changes, soreness and poor appetite may make eating difficult. Ask early for symptom and nutrition support.
New cough or breathlessness needs prompt assessment for infection, lung inflammation or a clot. Severe breathing difficulty or chest pain needs emergency help.

Blood tests check liver and kidney function and help the team review the dose. Report yellow skin or eyes, dark urine or right-sided upper abdominal pain. A changed creatinine result needs interpretation, not a self-directed dose change.
Take prescribed sickness support. Call if vomiting or diarrhoea persists, you cannot drink, or pain is severe.

Low red cells can cause tiredness or breathlessness; low white cells can increase infection risk; low platelets can cause bruising or bleeding. Persistent unexplained changes may need specialist marrow tests.
Report unusual bruising, bleeding, fever, shivers or suddenly feeling unwell. Do not wait for the next blood test.
A new painful swollen leg needs urgent assessment. Sudden chest pain or severe breathlessness is an emergency.
anatomy_note: Selected medicine-specific effects, not a prediction of what will happen to you. Symptoms can occur on any day, including during a prescribed pause.

urgent_extra: Call your oncology team urgently for fever, shaking chills, feeling suddenly unwell, unusual bruising or bleeding, marked weakness, new or worsening cough or breathlessness, a new painful swollen limb, yellow skin or eyes, dark urine, persistent vomiting or diarrhoea, or inability to keep fluids down. Follow your own temperature and contact plan; do not wait for the next appointment. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse, seizures or stroke symptoms: call 112/999.

sections.title: After chemotherapy and local treatment
sections.text: Olaparib follows the chemotherapy and local-treatment plan. In OlympiA, surgery and any indicated radiotherapy were completed before olaparib, with at least a two-week gap after local treatment. NCCP advises starting ideally within twelve weeks of the last surgery, chemotherapy or radiation; your team sets the start.

sections.title: Endocrine therapy may overlap
sections.text: For hormone receptor-positive disease, the prescribed hormone treatment can continue alongside olaparib and often continues after the one-year olaparib course. Its injections, tablets and bone checks keep their own schedule.

sections.title: A daily routine at home
sections.text: Choose consistent morning and evening times and check the strength and number of tablets on each new prescription. Keep a sufficient supply before weekends or holidays. No infusion pump or port is needed for olaparib itself.

sections.title: If treatment is paused
sections.text: The oncology team decides when and at what dose to restart after blood recovery or symptom improvement. Do not calculate a catch-up dose or restart automatically because a calendar month has passed.

sections.title: After the planned year
sections.text: Agree the stop date and ongoing breast follow-up. Endocrine treatment and breast surveillance may continue. Report persistent unexplained fatigue, infections, bruising or breathlessness even after olaparib finishes.

sections.title: Tablet strengths and missed doses
sections.text: Swallow the prescribed tablets whole with or without food, once in the morning and once in the evening. Do not chew, crush, dissolve or divide them. The usual starting dose is two 150 mg tablets each time (300 mg twice daily); your own dose may be lower. Check both tablet strength and tablet count after every prescription change. If you miss a dose, take the next normal dose at its usual time; do not double up. Do not substitute olaparib capsules for tablets. Avoid grapefruit juice and check other grapefruit or bitter-orange products with your pharmacist.

sections.title: Genetics and family questions
sections.text: BRCA1 and BRCA2 help repair damaged DNA. A germline change is present in the body’s cells and may have implications for relatives. A tumour-only change does not by itself show that it is inherited. Ask which test you had, what the result means and whether genetic counselling is appropriate. A variant of uncertain significance is not automatically a treatment-qualifying result.

evidence.title: OlympiA: benefit after one year of adjuvant treatment
evidence.intro: OlympiA compared one year of olaparib with placebo after chemotherapy and local treatment in 1,836 people with germline BRCA1/2-associated, high-risk HER2-negative early breast cancer.
evidence.population: NCCP 00588 h only: germline pathogenic BRCA1/2-associated HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer after neoadjuvant/adjuvant chemotherapy. Do not route other 00588 indications into this breast suite.
evidence.interpretation: At six years, estimated invasive disease-free survival was 79.6% with olaparib and 70.3% with placebo; estimated overall survival was 87.5% and 83.2%. Invasive disease-free survival counts specified invasive-cancer events or death, not just breast recurrence. These descriptive follow-up results support benefit after the planned one-year course; they do not mean six years of tablets or predict your personal outcome.
evidence.limitations: The result applies to the selected high-risk germline BRCA population. The trial predated routine neoadjuvant pembrolizumab and does not directly establish every modern treatment combination. Treatment burden, alternatives and rare late harms remain part of the discussion.

consent_support: Discuss the chance of reducing recurrence, the limits of trial averages, alternatives and your priorities. Review common effects and serious blood/marrow, lung, clotting, liver and allergic risks. Olaparib can harm an unborn baby. Discuss fertility and pregnancy prevention before treatment. If you could become pregnant, use two reliable complementary contraception methods during treatment and for six months after the last dose, following your team’s advice. A non-hormonal method may be needed because olaparib can reduce the effect of some hormonal contraceptives; hormone-sensitive cancer also affects the choice. Pregnancy testing is needed before treatment and may be repeated. Do not breastfeed during olaparib or for one month after the last dose. Tell the team immediately if pregnancy is possible. Use a condom during treatment and for three months after the last dose when having sex with a partner who is pregnant or could become pregnant. A partner who could become pregnant should also use highly effective contraception. Do not donate sperm during treatment or for three months afterwards; discuss fertility preservation before treatment if relevant.

support.title: Nausea support matched to oral treatment
support.text: Agree a written anti-sickness plan with your team, including what is prescribed regularly, what is for rescue, and when to call if it is not working. NCCP classifies oral olaparib as moderate-to-high sickness risk, but a fixed intravenous chemotherapy anti-sickness cycle does not apply. Some people need prescribed support and others do not need routine prevention. A stomach-acid medicine may be considered for symptoms under local policy.

support.title: Check the antiemetic interaction
support.text: Aprepitant is a moderate CYP3A inhibitor in NCCP 00588 and can increase olaparib exposure. The prescriber/pharmacist should choose and reconcile supportive medicines; never add an antiemetic from another regimen without checking.

support.title: Blood and infection support
support.text: Blood counts check red cells that carry oxygen, white cells that help fight infection and platelets that help stop bleeding. Low counts can lead to a pause, a lower prescribed dose, a transfusion or further tests. Persistent or unexplained changes sometimes need specialist bone-marrow tests to investigate myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukaemia (MDS/AML). These are serious conditions; their risk differs by treatment setting and previous therapy. A treatment pause is not itself a diagnosis. There is no universal routine white-cell growth-factor course.

support.title: Medicines and supplements
support.text: Give the pharmacist a complete list of prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines, vitamins and herbal products. Some antibiotics, antifungals, seizure medicines and St John’s wort can change how much olaparib reaches your body. Even anti-sickness treatment needs checking: aprepitant can increase olaparib exposure. Do not start a borrowed support medicine, change the olaparib dose or restart a paused course yourself.

support.title: Stomach symptoms
support.text: NCCP allows consideration of a proton pump inhibitor under local policy. This is symptom- and patient-dependent, rather than a compulsory medication for everyone.

support.title: If tablets are paused
support.text: Only the treating team can confirm when and at what dose to restart. Do not take catch-up doses after a pause.

support.title: Pregnancy, fertility and contraception
support.text: Olaparib can harm an unborn baby. Discuss fertility and pregnancy prevention before treatment. If you could become pregnant, use two reliable complementary contraception methods during treatment and for six months after the last dose, following your team’s advice. A non-hormonal method may be needed because olaparib can reduce the effect of some hormonal contraceptives; hormone-sensitive cancer also affects the choice. Pregnancy testing is needed before treatment and may be repeated. Do not breastfeed during olaparib or for one month after the last dose. Tell the team immediately if pregnancy is possible. Use a condom during treatment and for three months after the last dose when having sex with a partner who is pregnant or could become pregnant. A partner who could become pregnant should also use highly effective contraception. Do not donate sperm during treatment or for three months afterwards; discuss fertility preservation before treatment if relevant.

chapters.title: The exact treatment being discussed
chapters.intro: Reduce the chance of invasive recurrence after standard chemotherapy and local treatment. It may be taken alongside prescribed endocrine therapy for hormone receptor-positive disease.

items.title: Who this covers
items.text: Adults with a confirmed pathogenic germline BRCA1/2 mutation, HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer and previous neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy. The high-risk definition depends on hormone receptors, prior chemotherapy setting, surgical pathology and, for one pathway, CPS+EG score.

items.title: Dose and administration
items.text: Swallow the prescribed tablets whole with or without food, once in the morning and once in the evening. Do not chew, crush, dissolve or divide them. The usual starting dose is two 150 mg tablets each time (300 mg twice daily); your own dose may be lower. Check both tablet strength and tablet count after every prescription change. If you miss a dose, take the next normal dose at its usual time; do not double up. Do not substitute olaparib capsules for tablets. Avoid grapefruit juice and check other grapefruit or bitter-orange products with your pharmacist.

items.title: Duration and decisions
items.text: For breast indication 00588 h: up to one year, or earlier if the cancer recurs or side effects make treatment unsuitable. This is different from olaparib durations in ovarian, prostate and pancreatic cancer.

items.title: Individual safety and source differences
items.text: This patient suite is only for breast adjuvant indication 00588 h. Kidney/liver impairment, previous dose reductions and interacting medicines can change the dose. New blood abnormalities can occasionally signal a serious marrow problem and must be investigated.

chapters.title: Checks throughout treatment
chapters.intro: Blood tests assess treatment safety. Scans assess disease or investigate symptoms. Echo and ECG answer different questions.

items.title: Before treatment
items.text: Confirm the germline BRCA result and breast eligibility. Review blood count, kidney and liver tests, recovery from previous treatment, medicines and supplements, and pregnancy testing where relevant. Confirm the surgery/radiotherapy sequence and the planned start.

items.title: During treatment
items.text: NCCP specifies FBC, kidney and liver tests every four weeks for the first twelve months. Reviews also assess nausea, appetite, energy, bruising, infections and breathing symptoms. Extra tests or an interruption may be needed if results or symptoms change.

items.title: Heart checks
items.text: Olaparib alone has no routine electrocardiogram (ECG) or heart-ultrasound (echo) timetable in this NCCP regimen. Checks may still be needed because of previous treatment that can affect the heart, an existing condition or new symptoms.

items.title: Bone health
items.text: There is no olaparib-specific DXA schedule. If an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression is also prescribed, retain that treatment’s separate bone-density and bone-health plan.

chapters.title: Your wider treatment plan
chapters.intro: Additional treatments depend on the confirmed setting and indication.

items.title: Early-breast follow-up
items.text: After early breast cancer treatment, annual mammography is generally used for remaining breast tissue: both breasts after conservation, or the opposite breast after unilateral mastectomy. Routine mammography of the mastectomy side is not required. Routine CT, bone scans and tumour markers are not recommended solely to look for recurrence in an asymptomatic person. Safety blood tests for ongoing olaparib are a separate requirement. New symptoms need assessment between appointments.

items.title: Tumour markers
items.text: No routine tumour-marker surveillance for asymptomatic early breast cancer.

items.title: Pregnancy, fertility and contraception
items.text: Olaparib can harm an unborn baby. Discuss fertility and pregnancy prevention before treatment. If you could become pregnant, use two reliable complementary contraception methods during treatment and for six months after the last dose, following your team’s advice. A non-hormonal method may be needed because olaparib can reduce the effect of some hormonal contraceptives; hormone-sensitive cancer also affects the choice. Pregnancy testing is needed before treatment and may be repeated. Do not breastfeed during olaparib or for one month after the last dose. Tell the team immediately if pregnancy is possible. Use a condom during treatment and for three months after the last dose when having sex with a partner who is pregnant or could become pregnant. A partner who could become pregnant should also use highly effective contraception. Do not donate sperm during treatment or for three months afterwards; discuss fertility preservation before treatment if relevant.

chapters.title: Evidence depends on the population
chapters.intro: Different studies answer different questions; do not compare their results as if populations and follow-up were identical.

items.title: OlympiA: four-year survival analysis
items.text: The earlier survival update showed that the benefit extended beyond preventing invasive recurrence. These results apply to the selected high-risk inherited BRCA-associated early breast population, not every HER2-negative breast cancer.

items.title: OlympiA: sustained benefit at six years
items.text: Longer follow-up confirms that reductions in invasive recurrence and improvements in survival persist after the planned year of treatment. This is follow-up after one year of olaparib, not a longer prescribed course; rare late marrow effects still need attention.

chapters.title: Benefit, course and continuing checks
chapters.intro: In people with the high-risk inherited BRCA-associated breast cancer studied, one year of olaparib reduced invasive recurrence and improved survival. Longer follow-up shows that the benefit persists after treatment ends. Eligibility is specific, and benefit for an individual remains uncertain.

items.title: Before and during treatment
items.text: FBC, renal and liver profile every 4 weeks throughout the 12-month breast course; earlier/additional tests for symptoms or abnormal results. Review adherence, tablet supply, nausea, fatigue and all medicines.

items.title: Heart checks and the full course
items.text: No routine olaparib-specific ECG, echo or DXA; follow separate previous/ongoing treatment risks. Breast surveillance continues after olaparib, without automatic asymptomatic CT or tumour-marker scheduling. High risk:TNBC residual disease after neoadjuvant therapy or node-positive/≥2 cm after adjuvant chemotherapy; HR-positive disease requires residual disease with CPS+EG≥3 after neoadjuvant therapy or≥4 positive nodes after adjuvant chemotherapy. Ideally start within 12 weeks of the last surgery, chemotherapy or radiation.

chapters.title: Support and urgent symptoms
chapters.intro: Blood monitoring and a clear contact plan support treatment at home.

Low counts can lead to a pause, a lower prescribed dose, a transfusion or further tests. Persistent or unexplained changes sometimes need specialist bone-marrow tests to investigate myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukaemia (MDS/AML). These are serious conditions; their risk differs by treatment setting and previous therapy. A treatment pause is not itself a diagnosis.

items.text: Call your oncology team urgently for fever, shaking chills, feeling suddenly unwell, unusual bruising or bleeding, marked weakness, new or worsening cough or breathlessness, a new painful swollen limb, yellow skin or eyes, dark urine, persistent vomiting or diarrhoea, or inability to keep fluids down. Follow your own temperature and contact plan; do not wait for the next appointment. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse, seizures or stroke symptoms: call 112/999.

Even anti-sickness treatment needs checking: aprepitant can increase olaparib exposure. Do not start a borrowed support medicine, change the olaparib dose or restart a paused course yourself.

questions.q: When do I take or receive treatment?
questions.a: Take your prescribed olaparib dose morning and evening every day, without a planned rest week. This breast course lasts up to one year, or stops earlier if the cancer returns or side effects make treatment unsuitable. Prescribed endocrine therapy can continue on its own timetable. Swallow the prescribed tablets whole with or without food, once in the morning and once in the evening. Do not chew, crush, dissolve or divide them. The usual starting dose is two 150 mg tablets each time (300 mg twice daily); your own dose may be lower. Check both tablet strength and tablet count after every prescription change. If you miss a dose, take the next normal dose at its usual time; do not double up. Do not substitute olaparib capsules for tablets. Avoid grapefruit juice and check other grapefruit or bitter-orange products with your pharmacist.

questions.q: When are bloods, ECGs or echoes needed?
questions.a: Confirm the germline BRCA result and breast eligibility. Review blood count, kidney and liver tests, recovery from previous treatment, medicines and supplements, and pregnancy testing where relevant. Confirm the surgery/radiotherapy sequence and the planned start. NCCP specifies FBC, kidney and liver tests every four weeks for the first twelve months. Reviews also assess nausea, appetite, energy, bruising, infections and breathing symptoms. Extra tests or an interruption may be needed if results or symptoms change. Olaparib alone has no routine ECG or echo surveillance timetable in this NCCP regimen. Heart checks may still be needed because of previous anthracycline/HER2 treatment, existing disease or new symptoms.

After early breast cancer treatment, annual mammography is generally used for remaining breast tissue: both breasts after conservation, or the opposite breast after unilateral mastectomy. Routine mammography of the mastectomy side is not required. Routine CT, bone scans and tumour markers are not recommended solely to look for recurrence in an asymptomatic person. Safety blood tests for ongoing olaparib are a separate requirement. New symptoms need assessment between appointments.

For breast indication 00588 h: up to one year, or earlier if the cancer recurs or side effects make treatment unsuitable. This is different from olaparib durations in ovarian, prostate and pancreatic cancer.

questions.q: What should make me call today?
questions.a: Call your oncology team urgently for fever, shaking chills, feeling suddenly unwell, unusual bruising or bleeding, marked weakness, new or worsening cough or breathlessness, a new painful swollen limb, yellow skin or eyes, dark urine, persistent vomiting or diarrhoea, or inability to keep fluids down. Follow your own temperature and contact plan; do not wait for the next appointment. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse, seizures or stroke symptoms: call 112/999.
There is no olaparib-specific DXA schedule. If an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression is also prescribed, retain that treatment’s separate bone-density and bone-health plan.

questions.q: Does longer follow-up mean taking olaparib for longer?
questions.a: No. The OlympiA follow-up followed people after a planned year of treatment. Your breast course remains up to one year unless the team stops earlier.

For hormone receptor-positive disease, the prescribed hormone treatment can continue alongside olaparib and often continues after the one-year olaparib course. Its injections, tablets and bone checks keep their own schedule.

questions.q: Why does the inherited BRCA result matter?
questions.a: BRCA1 and BRCA2 help repair damaged DNA. A germline change is present in the body’s cells and may have implications for relatives. A tumour-only change does not by itself show that it is inherited. Ask which test you had, what the result means and whether genetic counselling is appropriate. A variant of uncertain significance is not automatically a treatment-qualifying result.

monitoring.test: Safety blood tests and symptom review
monitoring.when: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests every four weeks through the first 12 months; extra tests for symptoms or abnormal results. Review nausea, intake, fatigue, infection, bruising, breathing, medicines and tablet supply.

Continue the agreed breast follow-up and mammography plan. New symptoms need assessment. Olaparib safety blood tests are separate from surveillance; asymptomatic follow-up does not automatically require CT scans or tumour markers.

cycle_expectations: Symptoms may occur on any day; there is no planned rest week. Report new problems promptly.
Use only your prescribed sickness/rescue medicines. Call if vomiting, diarrhoea or poor intake persists; do not wait for the next review.
preparation: Confirm the germline BRCA1/2 result and high-risk HER2-negative breast indication, recovery from chemotherapy/local treatment, full blood count, kidney/liver tests, medicines and pregnancy testing where relevant.
Confirm tablet strength, supply, written support instructions and verified daytime/out-of-hours contact numbers.
patient_summary.card_schedule: Tablets twice daily; breast course up to one year.
patient_summary.card_record_note: Recording spaces do not define the planned course.
patient_summary.card_alert: Fever, suddenly unwell, unusual bleeding or new breathlessness: contact the team urgently. Severe symptoms: 112/999.

cycle_blocks.label: Every day
cycle_blocks.text: Morning and evening tablets at the prescribed dose; no planned rest week.

cycle_blocks.label: Between reviews
cycle_blocks.text: Keep the support plan and report symptoms promptly.

cycle_blocks.label: Next review
cycle_blocks.text: Check blood results, symptoms, supply and the next prescribed dose.

monitoring_test_details.label: Full blood count
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Check anaemia, infection risk and platelets; persistent changes may need further investigation.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before starting, then every four weeks throughout the one-year course, with extra tests when indicated.

monitoring_test_details.label: Kidney and liver tests
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Check organ function and whether the tablet prescription needs review.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before starting, then every four weeks in the first 12 months; earlier for concerning symptoms/results.

monitoring_test_details.label: Germline BRCA1/2 result
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Confirm the molecular requirement and discuss inherited/family implications.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Validated result before treatment; genetics discussion as appropriate.

monitoring_test_details.label: Pregnancy testing
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Avoid exposing an unborn baby to olaparib.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before treatment if you could become pregnant; repeat testing as advised.

monitoring_test_details.label: Mammography and breast follow-up
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Surveillance of remaining breast tissue and review of new symptoms.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Individual follow-up; annual mammography is generally recommended for remaining breast tissue. Other tests follow symptoms or individual risk.

monitoring_test_details.label: Heart and bone-density checks
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Monitor relevant previous treatment, endocrine therapy or existing risk; these are not a routine olaparib-only panel.
monitoring_test_details.timing: As indicated by the separate cardiac or endocrine/bone-health plan.
